text: No answer from the glass. But Nib finds an older way in: a narrow gap where the cables go.
Jaeha tells the crew they can wait here. Uncle Pyo didn't look for ten years. He's looking tonight.
Single file, they follow the cables down an old stone corridor.
And at its end, Jaeha stops dead. A tall iron door, propped open, violet light beyond it.
The colour drains out of the world.
Four years ago, a young Jaeha hammered on this same door with both fists.
Just inside it lies a rusted hard-hat lamp, and under it, a strip of faded orange vest.
Jaeha picks the lamp up, very gently.
Nib swings the door wider. Scratched deep into the iron inside: everyone comes back. And a little thumbs-up.
Jaeha drops to his knees and traces the letters. Minseok was alive in here, long enough to write it.
Nib rests a hand on his shoulder. Behind him, the crew take off their hard hats, one by one.
The trap-tester in the video, Moon Ahin says quietly. His hyung, says Jaeha. Now let's see what they shut this door on.
They crawl out onto an old stone balcony, and violet light rises over the balustrade like a sunrise.
Below is a pit a hundred and fifty metres wide, full of machinery. In its centre kneels a sea-giant in coral armour, chained, with dozens of pipes driven into his body.
A window reads like an inventory. Boss: the Hushed Tide Warden. Restrained, kept alive by machine. Core yield: four years, seventy-one days. Gate held open.
A tear of seawater runs down the giant's face.
The pipes pulse violet in time with his heartbeat.
In rows of glass tanks, the light settles into cores, each cap stamped with the hexagon and the crescent-moon seal.
Engineers work around him like dairy farmers. One leans on a chain, eating a sandwich.
So that's what the pipes are for, Uncle Pyo whispers.
Lyra's confidence is gone. The sea people sang about him on the river: the Warden who held back the tide.
Nib is shaking. That's a hero. They chained a hero and put taps in him.
Under Borro's hands, the stone balustrade cracks.
Moon Ahin raises her phone, and Jaeha lowers it. One flash, and every guard down there looks up.
A guard's torch sweeps up the wall toward them.
Everyone lies flat. Ho clamps both hands over his nose. The beam slides past.
Moon Ahin stares at the crescent seal on a tank. Half the hospitals in Seoul run on Kanghan cores.
And this is where they come from.
Jaeha writes out the rule: a gate stays open as long as its boss lives. Underneath, pressing so hard the paper tears: so they never let it die.
Nobody cleared this gate. They've been farming it for four years.
Through Nib's eyes, from under a catwalk, Jaeha studies the chain: black factory steel, with one small stamped mark.
From his pocket, he takes a small black chain link.
The last link of the knight's chains, when the rest crumbled to dust.
The same stamped mark. The knight at Gate 0912 wore the same chains. That gate was theirs too.
Nib drops back onto the balcony and freezes at the sight of it.
His voice cracks. His commander, the knight. The same people. The same chains.
His knives slide out. Jaeha grabs his wrist. Not yet. He promises. Not yet.
Trembling, Nib puts the knives away.
If this stops, Moon Ahin whispers, the hospitals go dark. Then somebody finds another way, says Jaeha. But not this way.
Uncle Pyo can't look again. They walked the traps for this, so the engineers could walk down safe.
Ho stares at his hands. The chicken shop money. Woo knows where it came from. Don't say it.
A freight elevator carries racks of glowing tanks up past them, toward the city.
Jaeha watches it rise, jaw tight, and thinks: every core in that lift is four years of his life.
Then the Warden's chained hand twitches, and the chain snaps taut against the wall.
The sandwich engineer jumps back and drops his lunch into the pit.
In the control room, the gauges swing into the red. Vitals are spiking. Something is agitating it.
The Warden's huge eyelid trembles.
He knows they're here, Borro whispers. How, Lyra asks. They haven't moved.
Jaeha understands. The giant can feel them, people from his own world, after four years alone.
On a monitor: three unregistered summons, on the old balcony, north wall.
An engineer jumps up and points straight at them.
Every light turns red, sirens wail, and guards run for the north wall. And the Warden's head lifts, just a fraction.
They know, says Moon Ahin. Everyone back to the door, Jaeha shouts. Husks first!
Black boots pound up a steel stair.
A guard captain orders the old passage locked. Nobody leaves level four.
Through Nib's eyes: torch beams filling the far end of the passage they came in by.
Lights below, lights behind, and every face on the balcony turns to Jaeha.
Across the pit, the Warden's eyelid lifts by a hair. Beneath it, a sliver of deep sea-green.
Jaeha opens his notebook to a blank page. Two minutes. He needs everybody to give him two minutes.
